description: Extends the predict-time TTA in _get_tta_logits from three shifted views to five (adds the top-right and bottom-left 2-pixel diagonal crops of the reflect-padded image), each also flipped, with all ten logit views averaged equally.

Replaces the fixed label smoothing of 0.09 with a linear schedule from 0.2 down to 0.0 over total_train_steps, passed into the compiled forward_step as a GPU tensor (filled each step) and applied through a manual smoothed cross-entropy that matches PyTorch's label_smoothing formula.
Wrap-pad the final training batch so all 50000 images appear each epoch, without changing the step budget.
Ramps the Muon momentum linearly from 0.5 at step 0 to MUON_MOMENTUM over the first 10 percent of total_train_steps by setting optimizer2's param group momentum each step before the optimizer step.

Replaces the linear-from-start LR decay with a trapezoidal schedule that holds both LR factors at 1 for the first 60 percent of total_train_steps and then decays them linearly to zero over the remaining 40 percent.
Adds nn.Dropout(0.1) on the flattened features just before the linear head, so it is active only in training mode and leaves predict() unchanged.

Replaces the fixed 1/256 logit division in CifarNet.forward with a learnable scalar head_scale (initialised to 1/in_features, reset in reset(), and added to the SGD head group) so the logit scale can adapt during training.

Keep the linear head and its scale in float32 so the large summed-loss gradients and head outputs cannot overflow half precision and produce NaN/inf logits; the cause is not verified, since I could not run the script.

Recalibrates BatchNorm running statistics on the test images (cumulative average, momentum None) inside predict(), then runs the usual TTA inference and restores the original BN buffers, so the model is unchanged after the call. An in-place save/restore replaces the deep copy because a deep copy of the torch.compile'd module would still call the original's compiled forward.

Adds a residual skip around conv2 in each ConvGroup (identity taken after the first SiLU, added after the second SiLU). No projection is needed because conv2 keeps channels_out, so the skip always matches shape and no parameters or optimizer groups change.

Progressive resolution: the first 40 percent of training steps downsample each augmented batch to 28x28 with bilinear antialiased interpolation, then train at full 32x32, leaving the whitening init, model, schedules and predict unchanged.

Progressive resolution: the first 40 percent of training steps downsample each augmented batch to 28x28 with bilinear antialiased interpolation, then train at full 32x32, leaving the whitening init, model, schedules and predict unchanged.
Disable the brightness and contrast color-jitter augmentation in the train() aug dict so batch_color_jitter is never called, keeping the 7.65-epoch budget unchanged.

Abort the mirror-only TTA idea: the prediction-time saving is only about 5000 fewer forward passes (roughly 0.5 percent of run time at best), and dropping the shifted views on the uncertain 25 percent likely costs more accuracy than that saves.
Removes the initial nn.GELU() from the start of CifarNet.layers so the whitening convolution feeds directly into the first ConvGroup; everything else is unchanged.

issues: No integrity problems: the diff only replaces the linear LR decay with a cosine decay. Nothing is carried between runs, nothing is seeded, no test data or file access is used, and the new imports (math cos and pi) are allowed.

Minor inconsistency, no veto: lr_factor1 is capped at progress 1.0 but lr_factor2 is not. If step*lr_factor2_base went past 1, the cosine would rise again. The old linear form would have gone negative at the same point, so that step is probably never reached, but the cap should be added for consistency.

Recomputed with job sd 0.026, 1 candidate run and 2 incumbent runs: the difference is +0.0104 (candidate worse), the standard error is 0.026*sqrt(1.5) = 0.0318, and |z| = 0.327. This matches the harness's -0.327 under its sign convention. The candidate is not better, so the provisional reject is consistent.

description: Replaces the linear-to-zero LR decay with cosine decay to zero for both optimizer groups: the whiten-bias group decays over its own whiten_bias_train_steps horizon (clamped at zero), and the norm-bias, head and Muon groups decay over total_train_steps.
Raises the training translation augmentation from 2 to 3 pixels and matches the predict-time TTA shift (pad 1 to 2, with the shifted crop offsets updated to fit).

Adds cutout to the training augmentation: each image has a 50% chance of having a random 8x8 square zeroed (to the mean colour, since it is applied after normalisation), applied in a small compiled helper inside CifarLoader.__iter__ after translation and flip and before colour jitter.

Three-stage resolution ramp: the first 40% of steps use bilinear antialiased resizing, the next 30% use 28x28, and the final 30% use full 32x32, with the first stage at 26x26 instead of the specified 24x24 because 24x24 fails in the MaxPool2d(3) at the end of the network.

Replaces the fixed Newton-Schulz coefficient triple in the Muon orthogonalisation with three Polar Express triples, one per unrolled iteration, leaving the magnitude scaling and transpose logic unchanged.

Replaces the Nesterov SGD optimizer1 with fused AdamW (betas 0.9/0.99, eps 1e-8) for the whiten bias, norm bias and head groups, with base lrs of 1e-3 and 2e-3 and decoupled weight decay WEIGHT_DECAY*BATCH_SIZE/lr; Muon for conv filters is unchanged.
Inserts a fixed depthwise 3x3 binomial blur (reflect-padded, half-precision buffer, channels_last) before each ConvGroup's MaxPool2d(2), leaving the final MaxPool2d(3) unchanged.
